body.text: Fri, 18 Sept, 7:50 pm, Final score, Tigers 0, Raiders 6
Dally M Awards live: Nathan Cleary and Tamika Upton favourites for NRL and NRLW honours
Rugby league crowns the best players in the game at tonight's Dally M Awards in Sydney, with Nathan Cleary and Tamika Upton favourites for the NRL and NRLW honours.

Speaking on the red carpet, Jai Arrow said he has not been given many details about a tribute to him that is set to take place just before the men's grand final on Sunday, in lieu of a pre-match entertainment act.
Follow every moment in our live blog below.

Your NRLW captain of the year is Kezie Apps
A huge cheer goes up as the Tigers skipper is announced, pipping Isabelle Kelly of the Roosters and the Titans' Georgia Hale.
Apps led the Tigers to their first finals series this year.
"I definitely don't deserve this with the amazing leaders we have in the women's game."
She hails the leadership group around her, and she's spot on. Raecene McGregor, Emily Bass, Holli Wheeler and Sarah Togatuki make for a very experienced bunch.
Karyn Murphy is the NRLW coach of the year
"I don't know if it's ever fun [being a coach].
"We've had a great year but equally shocked to be up here."
She wins the award after leading the Titans to second spot and within a few plays of another grand final.
A former star of the women's game when she and the Jillaroos had to pay their own way to the World Cup.
"Watching the women's game grow it seems quickly compared to how it was 10 years ago. It's not going anywhere, it's so exciting, the future."
Andrew Webster is the NRL coach of the year

I think everyone was expecting Justin Holbrook to win this after taking the Knights from last to seventh and into a grand final in his first year in Newcastle, but the Warriors mastermind gets the nod.
Again, hard to really argue considering what the Warriors did this year. Despite losing, among a lot more, halfbacks Luke Metcalf and Tanah Boyd, they still finished in the top two.
It's a shame that the season ended in straight sets in the finals but it shouldn't take away from everything Webster and the Wahs did this year.
Voli K sings in the In Memoriam montage
Millie Elliott named the Veronica White Woman of the Year
Retiring Roosters prop Millie Elliott started the Trainer Group Foundation to help get kids with special needs involved in sport.
"We don't do any of this work for these awards but it's special to be recognised."

Elliott's sister Hannah lives with down syndrome and her brother in law James has autism, and she says she has seen first-hand how sport can give kids like them so much fulfilment and a sense of community.
"When my little sister finished school I noticed that had faded away and I wanted to bridge that gap.
"Putting these programs on free of charge has been a dream of mine and something I'll be doing for a very long time."
Campbell Graham wins the Ken Stephen Medal
The Rabbitohs outside back has been honoured for his contribution to the community with his volunteering work with Vinnies.

"It's a huge honour. Across our game players always giving time and energy to their communities. I'm very proud to be part of a sport that gives to communities across the whole nation. It only takes a few people to make a difference in this world."
Graham says it was Jai Arrow who first brought him, and former teammate Liam Knight, to volunteer with Vinnies.
"Jai was doing Vinnies work well before me and he asked me to come along one night and we had an absolute ball.
"I know if your situation was diffrerent it'd be you up here and not me."
Graham says he hopes he can have a similar impact on younger teammates the same way Arrow did with him.
Ethan Sanders is the NRL rookie of the year
A tough year for the Raiders, slipping from minor premiers to outside the top eight, but definitely a deserving winner despite actually playing his first game back in 2024 for the Eels.
But his tutelage under Ricky Stuart is clearly paying off.
"It's a pretty famous jersey that Stick wore for a long time. Couldn't ask for a better coach."
Here are your NRL and NRLW tackles of the year
NRLW rookie of the year: Mercedez Taulelei-Siala
She looks genuinely stunned to win.
The Knights winger came straight out of school and into the NRLW and says her captain, Yasmin Meakes, and the rest of her teammates made it easy for her.
Next on the horizon is the World Cup with Samoa.
Edwards joins Cleary after round 18
The first batch of secret NRL votes have been revealed from round 13 to 18.
Sharks half Braydon Trindall makes a big move with 15 votes to climb into contention, but the big news is Penrith fullback Dylan Edwards joining Nathan Cleary atop the tally with 44 votes.

Raecene McGregor storms to top of NRLW tally after round eight

When NRLW voting went behind closed doors after round four, Tamika Upton had 12 points, with Roosters playmaker Tarryn Aiken (11), Raiders fullback Sheridan Gallagher (11), Brisbane halfback Jesse Southwell (10) and rugby sevens star turned Titans five-eighth Teagan Levi (9) trailing just behind.
We're about to receive our first batch of updates from the secret voting in rounds 5-8.
The Broncos had a dip here, but Tamika Upton does enough to nab seven votes.
Even so, she is bumped off top spot by Aiken and 2022 winner Raecene McGregor, who picked up 20 points to jump to top spot on 26 overall.
Aiken is next on 23 votes, with Upton on 19. Jess Sergis and NRLW rookie Teagan Levi are next on 18 and 16.
Joint top point-scorers
After 11 regular season games, what are the odds that two players would have scored exactly the same number of points — 98.
Also remarkable, Jocelyn Kelleher and Jesse Southwell both scored just one try each, making their hauls as goal-kickers a true testament to their teams' success this season.
Mackenzie Wiki wins NRLW try of the year
Frantic, frenetic and flashy, Mackenzie Wiki finished off this insane passage of play against the Gold Coast Titans in round nine.
Remarkably it was one of three she scored on the day.

If you want a more extensive wrap of the fashion and fits, Maddie Nixon has you covered.

With Nathan Cleary healing up at home, I'd imagine Ivan Cleary will be accepting it on his behalf.
Key Event
Jai Arrow awarded the Provan-Summons Medal
After a dramatic, inspiring and heartbreaking year, Jai Arrow has been handed the Provan-Summons Medal.
It's awarded to the player who has displayed the true spirit of the game, measured against four values: respect, honesty, bravery and sportsmanship.
Hard to argue with that one.
He's expected to be honoured again at the grand final on Sunday, but he says he has been told "nothing" about it.
Alex Johnston wins try of the year

There have been some spectacular tries scored this year, but I think the NRL is right to hand it to Alex Johnston for the long-range effort that broke Ken Irvine's record and sparked a pitch invasion.
Key Event
Ivan Cleary gives an update on Nathan
Heavy Dally M favourite Nathan Cleary is back home after the first of two surgeries.
He's had his left leg repaired after that gruesome compound fracture, and will be going back in to repair his broken right foot.
"He's pretty sore, but he's doing OK," dad and Panthers coach Ivan Cleary tells Fox Sports.
"He came home today. Back in Saturday for round two."
Ivan says it was a rough day for the whole Cleary clan on Sunday.
"It's a tough go, but it is what it is.
"Probably the first time in my coaching career with Nat where the line between dad and coach was a bit fuzzy."
As for Nathan's prospects of winning the top gong:
"I'm sure he'd be absolutely thrilled, it's a huge award. They don't play the game for individual awards and they'd much prefer to be on two legs in a grand final this week.
"That didn't work out, but of course if that happens he'd be stoked and we'd all be super proud."
